key_idea: Taking a prefix plus a suffix with sum q is the same as leaving behind a contiguous block with sum S - q, and since all values are positive a sliding window finds that in O(m).
sketch: Compute the total S. For a query q > S answer No; otherwise look for a contiguous subarray (possibly empty) with sum T = S - q using two pointers, shrinking from the left while the window exceeds T. Each query costs O(m), and m*n <= 1e7 keeps the total small; repeated targets are memoised. Pitfalls: q = 0 and q = S are both Yes (empty prefix/suffix or the whole roll), prefix and suffix may not overlap (automatic in the complement view), and the input has up to 1e6 lines so fast I/O is needed. Verified against an O(m^2) brute force.
